title: The Lost Phone
description: A story about a woman who leaves her phone on a bus and gets it back.
instructions: Read the text about a lost phone, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: Last Tuesday, Anna took the number 12 bus to work, like every day. She was very tired because she went to bed late the night before. She sat near the window and listened to music on her phone. After a few minutes, she put the phone on the seat next to her and closed her eyes.

Suddenly, the driver called out the name of her stop. Anna jumped up and ran off the bus. When she arrived at her office, she looked in her bag. Her phone was not there! She felt sick because all her photos and contacts were on it.

Anna borrowed a colleague's phone and called her own number. A man answered. 'Hello, I found this phone on the number 12 bus,' he said. His name was Tom, and he was a student. He agreed to meet Anna at a cafe near her office at lunchtime.

At one o'clock, Tom was waiting at the cafe with the phone. Anna was so grateful that she wanted to buy him lunch. Tom only wanted a cup of coffee. Since that day, Anna always keeps her phone in her bag on the bus.

While they drank their coffee, Anna and Tom talked for a long time. Tom studied music at the university, and he played the guitar in a small band. Anna told him that she loved music too. Before they left, Tom gave her a ticket for his band's concert on Saturday night.

On Saturday, Anna went to the concert with her friend Lucy. The band played in a small club in the city centre. The music was great, and the club was full of happy people. After the concert, Tom came to say hello. He told Anna that he usually takes the number 12 bus too, but in the evenings.

Now Anna and Tom are good friends. Sometimes they meet at the same cafe for lunch, and Anna always pays for the coffee now. Last month, she went to another concert and brought five colleagues with her. Anna often tells people the story of her lost phone. 'Losing my phone was a terrible moment,' she says, 'but it was also lucky. Without it, I never met Tom.'
